reason: E2 directly states that raising build space temperature is the most common approach to minimize cracking and that vertical cracks were expected due to the absence of preheating, supporting the link between pre-heating and defect reduction. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence on the CoCrFeNiMn alloy, the specific 500 °C temperature, the claimed quantitative improvements, or the absence of grain coarsening; E1 concerns a different alloy and process, and E3 is cited as conflicting but does not directly contradict the pre-heating premise.
premises: Pre-heating the build plate reduces thermal gradients and residual stresses in SLM
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses improve dimensional precision and reduce cracking/porosity
The benefit applies to equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn HEA processed by SLM
A pre-heat temperature of ~500 °C is sufficient and does not cause deleterious grain coarsening
The predicted improvements (30-50% dimensional reduction, 10-15% yield strength increase) are achievable
